summary: Adds an admin route that deletes one user by id and a bulk purge route that deletes a list of user ids.

findings.title: Delete user route lacks admin check
findings.description: The DELETE /users/:id handler omits the requireAdmin middleware that its sibling routes use. The router has no shared auth middleware, and server.js mounts it without auth. Any caller who reaches the server can delete any user by id. Unauthenticated callers can also delete users. Add requireAdmin to the route, as the GET /users and POST /users/purge routes do.

findings.fix: Add requireAdmin to the route, as the GET /users and POST /users/purge routes do.

findings.title: Purge deletions are never awaited
findings.description: The purge handler passes an async callback to forEach, so nothing awaits any removeUser promise. The handler responds with ids.length before any deletion finishes. removeUser throws for an unknown id, and that rejection goes unhandled and crashes the Node process. The client also gets a removed count that hides failed deletions. Await Promise.allSettled over the ids. Then report the count of fulfilled deletions.
findings.suggested_change:
const results = await Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => db.removeUser(id)));
  res.json({ removed: results.filter((r) => r.status === "fulfilled").length });

findings.title: New delete routes have no tests
findings.description: The change adds two routes that delete users. The repository has no test that covers either route. A regression in authorization or in deletion handling would go unnoticed. The missing admin check above is one example. Add tests for both routes. Cover the admin check, a partial purge failure and the reported removed count.
